mainTopic: Carrying amounts for bone, glass, and stone on שבת, and the rules for bathroom stones on שבת
overview: The משנה lists the minimum amounts of bone, glass, and stone that make a person liable for carrying them out on שבת, based on what each is useful for. The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה's 'key' seems bigger than the רבנן's 'spoon'. עולא answers that he means only the small teeth of a key, and a ברייתא follows about when key teeth and lock teeth can become טמא. The גמרא then gives another measure for glass and sets the stone thrown at an animal at ten זוז, big enough for the animal to feel it. Next it turns to stones carried into the bathroom on שבת. The חכמים, answering זונין, settle on 'a handful', and רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue over nut-sized or egg-sized stones, just as they do about an אתרוג. Further rules exclude crumbly פאייס, forbid using a stone in the normal weekday way, and allow a stone with marks of earlier use. A ברייתא warning that a used stone causes hemorrhoids is answered three ways. רב יוסף rules that a stone whose marks were blurred by rain is still allowed if the marks can be recognized, and a new question to רב begins that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: משנה: the minimum amount for a bone
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives the amount of bone that makes one liable: enough to make a spoon. רבי יהודה says: enough to make a key.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A bone: enough to make a spoon. רבי יהודה says: enough to make a key out of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells us how much bone a person must carry out on שבת to be liable. There are two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת you are only liable for carrying something that is a useful amount. The תנא קמא measures bone by whether it could be made into a spoon. רבי יהודה measures it by whether it could be made into a key.

keyTerms.meaning: Key (or the teeth of a key)

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
A bone: enough to make a spoon.
phrases.notes: This is the minimum amount for liability when carrying it out.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Enough to make a key out of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of carrying amounts from the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bone: liable for enough to make a spoon. According to רבי יהודה, enough to make a key.

steps.title: משנה: the minimum amount for glass
steps.stepSummary: The amount of glass is enough to scrape the tip of a weaver's stick.
steps.simpleTranslation: Glass: enough to scrape with it the top of a weaver's stick.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the minimum amount of glass that makes one liable for carrying it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A piece of glass is useful for scraping and smoothing the tip of a כַּרְכֵּר, a pointed stick that weavers use. Even a small shard is good for this, so the amount is small.

keyTerms.meaning: A pointed stick used in weaving

phrases.english: Glass: enough to scrape with it
the top of a weaver's stick.

steps.triggerLanguage: זְכוּכִית כְּדֵי לִגְרוֹר בָּהּ רֹאשׁ הַכַּרְכֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next item in the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Glass: liable for enough to scrape the tip of a weaver's stick.

steps.title: משנה: the minimum amount for a pebble or stone
steps.stepSummary: A stone must be big enough to throw at a bird. רבי אלעזר בר יעקב says it must be big enough to throw at an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: A pebble or a stone: enough to throw at a bird. רבי אלעזר בר יעקב says: enough to throw at an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the minimum size of a stone, and there are two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People throw stones to chase animals away. A bird is scared off by a small stone, so the תנא קמא's amount is small. An animal such as a cow needs a bigger stone, so רבי אלעזר בר יעקב's amount is larger.

phrases.aramaic: צְרוֹר אוֹ אֶבֶן — כְּדֵי לִזְרוֹק בָּעוֹף.
phrases.english: A pebble or a stone: enough to throw at a bird.
Rabbi Elazar bar Yaakov says:
Enough to throw at an animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: צְרוֹר אוֹ אֶבֶן כְּדֵי לִזְרוֹק בָּעוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last item in this part of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stone: liable for enough to throw at a bird. According to רבי אלעזר בר יעקב, enough to throw at an animal.

steps.title: Why is רבי יהודה's amount larger here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה's amount (a key) is bigger than the רבנן's (a spoon), when we normally hold that the רבנן's amount is the bigger one.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Is that to say that רבי יהודה's amount is larger? But we hold that the רבנן's amount is larger!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the bone dispute in the משנה. A key seems bigger than a spoon, which goes against the usual pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We have an established assumption that in these disputes the רבנן have the larger amount and רבי יהודה the smaller one. A full key seems to need more bone than a small spoon. That would give רבי יהודה the larger amount, making him the more lenient one here, which reverses the usual pattern. So the גמרא asks how this can be.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (introduces a surprising implication)
We hold / it is established for us

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Is that to say that Rabbi Yehuda's measure is larger?

phrases.aramaic: הָא קַיְימָא לַן דְּשִׁיעוּרָא דְרַבָּנַן נְפִישׁ!
phrases.english: But we hold that the Rabbis' measure is larger!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the bone dispute from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's amount for bone ('enough to make a key')
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A key needs more bone than a spoon. That goes against the established rule that the רבנן's amount is larger than רבי יהודה's.

steps.title: עולא: רבי יהודה means only the teeth of a key
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that רבי יהודה's 'חף' means just the teeth of a key, which are small.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: the teeth of a key.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the question by explaining what רבי יהודה's word חף really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה is not talking about a whole key. He means the small teeth of a key, the part that catches the lock. That takes less bone than a spoon, so the usual pattern holds: the רבנן's amount is larger.

phrases.english: Ulla said: the teeth of a key.
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה means a small amount, the teeth only.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines a term in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חף means a whole key, which is bigger than a spoon.
steps.terutzMaskana: חף means only the teeth of a key, which are smaller than a spoon. So the רבנן's amount stays the larger one.
steps.whatToRemember: In the bone dispute, רבי יהודה's 'key' means just the small teeth of a key. That keeps his amount smaller than the רבנן's.

steps.title: ברייתא: when key teeth can become impure
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that loose key teeth are טהור, but once attached to a key they can become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: key teeth are pure. If one attached them to a key, they are impure.
steps.whatsHappening: Since עולא mentioned key teeth, the גמרא brings a related ברייתא about whether they can become ritually impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Loose teeth are not a working utensil on their own, so they cannot receive טומאה. Once fixed onto a key, they are part of a utensil and can become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Pure; here, unable to become impure

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The teeth of a key are pure;
phrases.notes: On their own they are not a complete utensil.

phrases.english: if one fixed them in the key, they are impure (susceptible).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side discussion triggered by עולא's term 'חפי פותחת'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Loose key teeth cannot become טמא. Once fixed to a key, they can.
steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא is not about carrying on שבת. It is a side point about טומאה, brought in only because עולא mentioned key teeth.

steps.title: ברייתא: lock teeth attached to a door stay pure
steps.stepSummary: The teeth of a lock (גל) stay טהור even when nailed to a door, because anything attached to the ground is treated like the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: And lock teeth, even though one attached them to the door and fixed them with nails, are pure, because anything attached to the ground is like the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a contrasting case: lock parts fixed to a door. These never become susceptible to טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earth itself cannot become טמא. A door is attached to a building, which is attached to the ground. So anything fixed to the door counts as part of the ground and stays טהור, even though it is attached to something.

keyTerms.meaning: A lock (bolt mechanism fixed on a door)

phrases.english: And those (teeth) of a lock,
even though one attached them to the door
and fixed them with nails, are pure,
because anything attached to the ground
is like the ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁל גַּל אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחִיבְּרָן בַּדֶּלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 6. Being attached to a key makes the teeth susceptible, but being attached to a door does not.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lock teeth fixed to a door are טהור, because anything attached to the ground is like the ground.
steps.whyThisMatters: 'כל המחובר לקרקע הרי הוא כקרקע' is a basic rule found all over ש"ס. Things fixed to the ground share the ground's status.

steps.title: Another version of the glass amount
steps.stepSummary: A תנא gives a different measure for glass: enough to cut two threads at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: Glass: enough to scrape with it. A תנא taught: glass, enough to cut two threads at once with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה's line about glass and quotes a ברייתא that measures it differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה measures glass by its use for scraping. The ברייתא measures it by its use as a cutting tool: a glass shard sharp enough to cut two threads at once, like a small knife.

phrases.english: Glass: enough to scrape with it.
A tanna taught: glass:

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי לִפְצוֹעַ בָּהּ שְׁנֵי נִימִין כְּאַחַת.
phrases.english: enough to cut two threads at once with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא סְכוּכִית כְּדֵי לִפְצוֹעַ בָּהּ שְׁנֵי נִימִין כְּאַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה's glass clause from step 2, after the side discussion about key teeth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the ברייתא, the amount of glass is enough to cut two threads at once.

steps.title: The animal must actually feel the stone
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains רבי אלעזר בר יעקב: the stone must be big enough that the animal feels it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A pebble or stone: enough to throw at a bird. רבי אלעזר etc. רבי יעקב said in the name of רבי יוחנן: and that is only when the animal feels it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the stone dispute in the משנה and adds a condition to רבי אלעזר בר יעקב's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not enough to throw something at an animal. The stone has to be heavy enough that the animal feels it and reacts. That makes the amount clearer and larger.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc. (the quote continues as in the משנה)

phrases.aramaic: צְרוֹר אוֹ אֶבֶן כְּדֵי לִזְרוֹק בָּעוֹף.
phrases.english: A pebble or a stone: enough to throw at a bird.
Rabbi Elazar etc. (says: enough to throw at an animal).

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yaakov said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
And that is only when it (the animal) feels it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְהוּא שֶׁמַּרְגֶּשֶׁת בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the stone clause from step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר בר יעקב, the stone must be big enough that the animal feels it.

steps.title: How heavy is that stone?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact size of a stone that an animal would feel.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is its measure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question to turn 'the animal feels it' into an exact amount. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Big enough that the animal feels it' is vague. The גמרא wants a fixed weight.

keyTerms.meaning: And how much is its measure?

phrases.english: And how much is its measure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for an exact measure for רבי יוחנן's condition.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact weight of a stone that an animal would feel.

steps.title: The stone weighs ten זוז
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי אלעזר בן יעקב himself: the stone must weigh ten זוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אלעזר בן יעקב says: a weight of ten זוז.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא that gives the weight in רבי אלעזר בן יעקב's own words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זוז is a coin, also used as a unit of weight. A stone weighing ten זוז is the size an animal will feel, so that is the amount for liability according to רבי אלעזר בן יעקב.

keyTerms.meaning: A silver coin, also used as a unit of weight

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Elazar ben Yaakov says:
A weight of ten zuz.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר מִשְׁקַל עֲשָׂרָה זוּז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The stone must weigh ten זוז.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר בן יעקב, one is liable for carrying out a stone big enough to throw at an animal and be felt by it. That is a stone weighing ten זוז.

steps.title: זונין asks the size of bathroom stones
steps.stepSummary: זונין comes into the בית מדרש and asks the חכמים how big the bathroom stones may be on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: זונין entered the בית מדרש and said to them: My teachers, the stones used in the bathroom, how big are they allowed to be?
steps.whatsHappening: A man named זונין asks the חכמים a practical question. On שבת, how big may the stones be that a person carries into the bathroom for wiping?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stones are normally מוקצה on שבת, but the חכמים allowed them for bathroom use because of כבוד הבריות, human dignity. זונין wants to know the size limit of that permission.

keyTerms.meaning: My teachers, a respectful way to address the Sages

phrases.english: Zunin entered the study hall,
he said to them: My teachers,
stones of the bathroom,
how much is their measure?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָנִים שֶׁל בֵּית הַכִּסֵּא שִׁיעוּרָן בְּכַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from stones used as tools to the size of bathroom stones on שבת
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The size limit for bathroom stones that may be carried on שבת

steps.title: The Sages answer with three exact sizes
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say the stones may be the size of a כזית, a כאגוז, or a כביצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: the size of an olive, the size of a nut, or the size of an egg.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים answer זונין by giving three exact measurements.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their first answer sets clear, precise sizes. The next step will challenge whether such precise sizes make sense in real life.

phrases.english: They said to him:
an olive-bulk, a nut-bulk, and an egg-bulk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers זונין's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three exact sizes: olive, nut, and egg

steps.title: זונין objects: nobody brings scales to the bathroom
steps.stepSummary: זונין asks whether a person is expected to bring scales into the bathroom to measure the stones.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Is a person supposed to bring scales into the bathroom?
steps.whatsHappening: זונין pushes back on the answer. Exact sizes are impractical, because nobody measures stones before using the bathroom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is phrased as a question, but it works as a challenge. A rule that needs exact measuring does not fit a situation where a person needs stones quickly.

keyTerms.meaning: And is it really so? It introduces a rhetorical challenge

phrases.english: He said to them:
And will he bring scales in?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule of three exact sizes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Exact measurements cannot work in practice, because no one weighs stones in a bathroom

steps.title: The Sages vote: a handful
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים take a vote and decide that a handful of stones is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: They took a vote and concluded: a full handful.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים accept זונין's point. They vote and set the rule as 'a handful' instead of exact sizes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exact measurements are replaced by a simple, practical measure. A person just grabs a handful and does not need to check sizes.

phrases.english: They voted and concluded:
a full handful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves זונין's objection
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The measure for bathroom stones on שבת is a handful

steps.title: A ברייתא records both positions
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records רבי יוסי giving the three sizes and his son quoting him as saying 'a handful'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יוסי says an olive, a nut, and an egg. רבי שמעון son of רבי יוסי says in his father's name: a handful.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא backs up the story. It shows the same two opinions, the three sizes and 'a handful', in the names of רבי יוסי and his son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two answers in the זונין story match two versions of רבי יוסי's view. This supports the final ruling of 'a handful'.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of his father

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
an olive-bulk, a nut-bulk, and an egg-bulk.
Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi Yosei
says in the name of his father: a handful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that matches the story
steps.raayaObject: The two positions, three sizes or a handful
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי יוסי and his son

steps.title: Three sharpened stones: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה disagree on size
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא allows three sharp-edged stones in the bathroom on שבת. רבי מאיר says they may be the size of a nut, and רבי יהודה says the size of an egg.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught regarding שבת: three sharp-edged stones may be brought into the bathroom. How big? רבי מאיר says: like a nut. רבי יהודה says: like an egg.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא gives a different rule. A person may bring three sharp stones, and two תנאים disagree about their size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number of stones is fixed at three, and the size is disputed. רבי מאיר allows nut-sized stones, and רבי יהודה allows larger, egg-sized ones.

keyTerms.meaning: It is permitted to bring in

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught regarding Shabbat:
three sharp-edged stones
may be brought into the bathroom.
And how big are they?
Rabbi Meir says: like a nut.
Rabbi Yehuda says: like an egg.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another ברייתא about the size of bathroom stones
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three sharp stones are allowed. רבי מאיר says nut-sized, and רבי יהודה says egg-sized

steps.title: רב חסדא: the same dispute as with אתרוג
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says that this מחלוקת matches their מחלוקת about the minimum size of an אתרוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם בר פפא said in the name of רב חסדא: Just like the dispute here, so is the dispute about an אתרוג.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא links this מחלוקת to a similar one. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה also disagree about how big an אתרוג must be, nut-sized or egg-sized.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works as a memory aid that connects two places where the same pair argues over the same two sizes. The wording here makes the bathroom-stone case the main reference point.

keyTerms.meaning: Citron, used for the מצוה on סוכות

phrases.english: Rafram bar Pappa said
that Rav Chisda said:
Like the dispute here,
so is the dispute about an etrog.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the ברייתא's dispute to another dispute
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bathroom-stone dispute matches the אתרוג dispute

steps.title: The comparison is backwards
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the אתרוג case is a well-known משנה, while this case is only a ברייתא, so the comparison should go the other way.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is a משנה, here it is a ברייתא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges how רב חסדא phrased his comparison. You should compare the lesser-known source to the famous one, not the other way around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה is better known than a ברייתא. So the אתרוג משנה should be the reference point, and this ברייתא should be compared to it.

keyTerms.meaning: A משנה, the main, well-known text
A ברייתא, a teaching left outside the משנה

phrases.english: There it is a Mishnah,
here it is a Baraita!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רב חסדא's comparison
steps.kashyaTarget: The direction of רב חסדא's comparison
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The famous source (a משנה) should be the anchor, not the less-known ברייתא

steps.title: The corrected wording
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reverses the wording: just like the dispute about the אתרוג, so is the dispute here.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: Just like the dispute about an אתרוג, so is the dispute here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording so that the famous אתרוג משנה is the reference point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The content stays the same, and only the order of the comparison changes. Now the ברייתא is explained in light of the משנה.

phrases.english: Rather:
Like the dispute about an etrog,
so is the dispute here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by fixing the wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was the anchor of the comparison
steps.terutzMaskana: The אתרוג משנה is the anchor, and the ברייתא is compared to it

steps.title: רב יהודה: not the פאייס
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says that 'פאייס' may not be carried into the bathroom on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: But not the פאייס.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה adds an exception. Some material called פאייס is not included in the permission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission covers real stones. רב יהודה excludes one item, and the גמרא will next ask what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: A crumbly material, explained in the next steps

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
But not the payis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the permission for bathroom stones
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פאייס may not be carried for bathroom use on שבת

steps.title: What is פאייס?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word פאייס means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is פאייס?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of an unfamiliar word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We cannot apply רב יהודה's rule until we know what material he is excluding.

phrases.english: What is 'payis'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a word in רב יהודה's rule

steps.title: רבי זירא: Babylonian clods
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that פאייס means crumbly clods of Babylonian earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Babylonian clods of earth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא defines פאייס as soft, flaky lumps of Babylonian earth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These clods crumble easily, so they do not work like real stones. That is why the permission does not cover them.

keyTerms.meaning: Clods of Babylonian earth that crumble easily

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
Babylonian clods.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the word
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: פאייס are crumbly clods of Babylonian earth

steps.title: רבא: no weekday-style use of a stone on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבא forbids using a stone on שבת to help with relieving oneself in the normal weekday way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is forbidden to rub with a stone on שבת the way one rubs on a weekday.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a limit on how a stone may be used. A person may not use it on שבת to help with relieving himself the way he normally would during the week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new rule about the manner of use, not about size. Doing it the usual weekday way is forbidden on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: To rub or press, here to help the body relieve itself

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is forbidden to rub with a stone on Shabbat
the way one rubs on a weekday.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new rule about how a stone may be used
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stone may not be used on שבת to help relieve oneself in the normal weekday way

steps.title: מר זוטרא: should he endanger himself?
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא objects that holding back from relieving oneself is dangerous.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא challenged it: Should he put himself in danger?
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא challenges רבא. If the person cannot relieve himself, he could be in danger, so how can we forbid this?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holding back bodily needs can be harmful to health. A rule that leads to danger seems unacceptable.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra challenged it:
Should he endanger himself?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's rule
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ban on using a stone on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Forbidding it could cause danger to health

steps.title: Do it in an unusual way
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that he should do it כלאחר יד, in an unusual way.
steps.simpleTranslation: In an unusual manner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבא's meaning. The person may do it, but in an unusual way and not the normal weekday way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא never forbade the act completely. He only required a change in how it is done, so there is no danger and שבת is still respected.

keyTerms.meaning: In an unusual way, literally 'with the back of the hand'

phrases.english: In an unusual manner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers מר זוטרא's challenge
steps.terutzMaskana: It is allowed when done in an unusual way
steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not forbid the act itself. He only forbids doing it in the regular weekday way.

steps.title: רבי ינאי: fixed bathroom or not
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי says that with a fixed bathroom a handful is allowed. Without one, a person may use a stone about the size of a small spice mortar.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי said: If there is a fixed place for the bathroom, a handful. If not, a stone the size of a small spice mortar.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי gives two different size rules. The rule depends on whether the person has a fixed bathroom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a fixed bathroom, leftover stones can be used another time, so carrying a handful is fine. Without a fixed place, he takes one medium-sized stone, about the size of a small spice mortar.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai said:

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ מָקוֹם קָבוּעַ לְבֵית הַכִּסֵּא —
phrases.english: If there is a fixed place for the bathroom —
a handful.
If not —
the average size of a small spice mortar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the question of size and adds a new distinction
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fixed bathroom: a handful. No fixed bathroom: one stone the size of a small spice mortar

steps.title: רב ששת: a stone with signs of use is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says that a stone showing signs of earlier bathroom use is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: If it has a mark on it, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת says a stone that clearly was already used in the bathroom may be carried for that use on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The marks show the stone is set aside for bathroom use, so it is allowed no matter its size. This ruling sets up the challenge that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: A sign or mark, literally 'a witness'

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
If it has a mark on it, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another case where a stone is allowed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stone with signs of earlier bathroom use is permitted on שבת

steps.title: A used stone causes hemorrhoids
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists ten things that cause hemorrhoids, including wiping with a stone someone else used. This challenges רב ששת.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: Ten things bring a person to hemorrhoids: eating reed leaves, grape leaves, vine tendrils, an animal's palate without salt, a fish's spine, salted fish not fully cooked, drinking wine dregs, wiping with lime or clay, and wiping with a stone his friend wiped with. Some say also one who suspends himself in the bathroom, without sitting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ששת. A ברייתא says that wiping with a used stone is unhealthy, so how can he allow it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת permits a stone that shows earlier use. The ברייתא says a stone used by someone else causes hemorrhoids, which makes it dangerous.

keyTerms.meaning: One who wipes or cleans himself

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Ten things bring a person
to hemorrhoids, and these are they:
one who eats reed leaves,
grape leaves, and vine tendrils,
and an animal's palate without salt,
and the spine of a fish,

phrases.aramaic: וְדָג מָלִיחַ שֶׁלֹּא בִּישֵּׁל כׇּל צוֹרְכּוֹ,
phrases.english: and salted fish not fully cooked,
and one who drinks wine dregs,
and one who wipes with lime, or with clay,
and one who wipes with a stone his friend wiped with.
And some say:
also one who suspends himself in the bathroom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת from a ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's permission to use a stone with signs of use
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says wiping with a used stone causes hemorrhoids, so such a stone should not be used

steps.title: First answer: moist versus dry
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a moist used stone. רב ששת is talking about a dry one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this is when it is moist, this is when it is dry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two sources describe different cases. A moist used stone is harmful, and a dry one is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a used stone has dried, it is no longer harmful. So רב ששת's permission applies to a dried stone.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult, introducing an answer

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is when moist, this is when dry.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּלַח, הָא בְּיָבֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a moist used stone is harmful, and a dry one is allowed

steps.title: Second answer: same side versus other side
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: the ברייתא means using the same used side. רב ששת allows using the other side.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: here it is one side, here it is both sides.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to settle the challenge. It splits the case by which side of the stone is used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wiping with the side that was already used is harmful. Using the other, clean side of the stone is fine, and that is the case רב ששת permits.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say, introducing another answer

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
here it is from one side,
and here it is from both sides.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the same challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (which side of the stone)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any use of a used stone is harmful
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the already-used side is harmful, and the other side is allowed

steps.title: Third answer: his own stone versus his friend's
steps.stepSummary: A third answer: a person's own used stone is allowed. Someone else's used stone is harmful.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: this is his own, this is his friend's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a third answer. It splits the case by whose stone it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא specifically says 'a stone his friend wiped with'. So רב ששת's permission can refer to a person's own stone, which is not harmful to him.
steps.whatToRemember: Bathroom stones on שבת are measured by a handful, and soft clods (פאייס) are excluded. A stone may not be used in the regular weekday way. A used stone is allowed (רב ששת), and the warning about hemorrhoids applies only to a moist stone, the used side, or someone else's stone.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
this is his own, this is his friend's.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָא דִּידֵיהּ, הָא דְּחַבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third answer to the same challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (whose stone it is)
steps.terutzMaskana: Only someone else's used stone is harmful, and one's own is allowed

steps.title: What if rain blurred the marks on the stone?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף about a used bathroom stone whose marks were blurred by rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: If rain fell on the stone and the marks were blurred, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks a new practical question. A stone has signs that it was used in the bathroom, but rain fell and blurred those signs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The marks of earlier use show that the stone is set aside for bathroom use. That is why it may be moved on שבת. If rain blurs those marks, the stone may no longer look like a bathroom stone, and it could become an ordinary מוקצה stone.

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
If rain fell on it (the stone)
phrases.notes: The stone that shows it was used before

phrases.english: and they (the marks) became blurred, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב ששת's rule (Step 28) that a stone with marks of earlier use is permitted. Now the question is whether the rule still holds once those marks are blurred.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a used stone keep its permitted status if rain blurs the marks of its earlier use?

steps.title: If the marks are still visible, the stone is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that if the marks can still be recognized, the stone may be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If their marks can still be recognized, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי. As long as you can still see the marks, the stone stays permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The marks do not need to be perfectly clear. They only need to be recognizable, so that the stone is still known as a bathroom stone. The answer implies that if the marks are completely gone, the stone would not be permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: A used bathroom stone keeps its permitted status as long as its marks can still be recognized, even if rain partly blurred them.

phrases.english: He (Rav Yosef) said to him:
If their marks are still recognizable, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִם הָיָה רִישּׁוּמָן נִיכָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers אביי's question from Step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: If the marks are still recognizable, the stone stays permitted. Partial blurring does not matter.

steps.title: A new question is asked of רב
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב שילא begins asking רב a question. The question itself continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב שילא asked רב:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It introduces a new question from רבה בר רב שילא to רב, and the content of the question comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far this step only tells us who is asking whom. The phrase בעא מיניה signals that a real question is coming. We will see its details on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: he asked him (introduces a question put to a teacher)

steps.confusionAlert: This is only the opening line. Don't look for the question here, because it starts on the next amud.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבָּהּ בַּר רַב שֵׁילָא מֵרַב
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Sheila asked of Rav
phrases.notes: The question continues on the next amud

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבָּהּ בַּר רַב שֵׁילָא מֵרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question after רב יוסף's answer. Its content continues on the next amud.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Not yet stated. The question continues on the next amud.
